topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Besides notifying the Commission in writing within the required timeframe, what else must a salesperson or associate broker do when changing employment to a new broker, under RELRA Section 603(a)?
choice_a: Pay the required fee and return the current license to the Commission
choice_b: Obtain a notarized release from the former broker
choice_c: File a separate application with the new broker's E&O insurer
choice_d: Post a public notice of the change in a local newspaper
explanation: RELRA Section 603(a) requires a salesperson or associate broker changing employment to notify the Commission in writing no later than ten days after the intended date of change, pay the required fee, and return the current license.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.603(a) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: During the interim period after a salesperson or associate broker changes employing brokers but before the new license arrives, RELRA Section 603(a) says the licensee's temporary license consists of what?
choice_a: The copy of the notification of change sent to the Commission
choice_b: A verbal confirmation from the new broker
choice_c: The old, returned license, which remains valid for 90 more days
choice_d: A temporary permit issued instantly online by the Commission
explanation: Section 603(a) provides that during the interim following a change in affiliation, the licensee 'shall maintain a copy of the notification sent to the commission as his temporary license pending receipt of his new current license.'
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.603(a) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under RELRA Section 603(a), what specifically prompts the Commission to issue a salesperson or associate broker's new license after a change of employment?
choice_a: Receipt by the Commission of the new broker's acknowledgment of the change of employment
choice_b: The passage of exactly 30 days from the date of change
choice_c: Payment of the fee alone, with no input needed from the new broker
choice_d: Completion of a background check by the new broker
explanation: Section 603(a) states: 'The commission, shall, upon receipt of acknowledgment from the new broker of the change of employment issue a new license.'
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.603(a) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: RELRA Section 603(b), addressing campground membership and time-share salespersons, describes their relationship to a broker using which verb, in contrast to Section 603(a)'s language for ordinary salespersons?
choice_a: 'Supervised by,' rather than 'employed by'
choice_b: 'Sponsored by'
choice_c: 'Contracted with'
choice_d: 'Licensed under'
explanation: Section 603(b) states no campground membership or time-share salesperson 'shall be supervised by any other broker than is designated upon the current license,' using 'supervised' rather than the 'employed' language of subsection (a) -- although the same change-of-broker notice procedure applies to both.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.603(b) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under RELRA Section 604(a), how may a disciplinary proceeding against a licensee be initiated?
choice_a: Either on the Commission's own motion, or promptly upon a verified written complaint from any person
choice_b: Only by a majority vote of all real estate brokers in the county
choice_c: Only after a criminal conviction has already occurred
choice_d: Only by the Attorney General's office, never by the Commission itself
explanation: Section 604(a) provides the commission may act 'upon its own motion' and 'shall promptly upon the verified complaint in writing of any person' ascertain the facts and, if warranted, hold a hearing.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(a) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: RELRA Section 604(5.1) makes which conduct a disciplinable prohibited act?
choice_a: Failing to comply with any of the requirements of Section 608.5 (handling of deposits and other escrows)
choice_b: Failing to renew continuing education within 5 years
choice_c: Failing to display a real estate license number on business cards
choice_d: Failing to join a local multiple listing service
explanation: Section 604(5.1), added in 2009 alongside the escrow overhaul, directly makes any failure to comply with Section 608.5's escrow-handling requirements an independently disciplinable prohibited act.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(5.1) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: RELRA Section 604(12)'s bar on accepting a commission from anyone other than the employing broker applies to which classes of licensee?
choice_a: Both salespersons and associate brokers
choice_b: Only salespersons, never associate brokers
choice_c: Only associate brokers, never salespersons
choice_d: Only cemetery salespersons
explanation: Section 604(12) applies its commission-source restriction to 'a salesperson or associate broker' alike -- both classes may receive a commission for licensed acts only from their employing broker.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(12) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: A broker pays a $500 'marketing consulting fee' to an unlicensed friend who brought in a buyer, instead of paying a commission to a licensed cooperating broker. Under RELRA Section 604(12.1), is this permitted?
choice_a: No -- a broker may not pay a commission or other valuable consideration for licensed acts to anyone other than the broker's own licensed employees or another real estate broker
choice_b: Yes, as long as it is labeled a 'consulting fee' rather than a commission
choice_c: Yes, up to $1,000 per referral
choice_d: Yes, if the unlicensed friend signs an independent contractor agreement
explanation: Section 604(12.1) bars a broker from paying a commission or other valuable consideration to anyone but the broker's own licensed employees or another licensed broker for performing licensed acts -- relabeling the payment as a 'consulting fee' does not change the substance of the transaction.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(12.1) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: A broker's own license lapses for non-renewal, but the broker continues to negotiate a sale for a client anyway. Which RELRA prohibited-acts provision does this most directly violate?
choice_a: Section 604(21) -- performing any act for which a real estate license is required when the actor's license is not currently in effect
choice_b: Section 604(9) -- failing to furnish a copy of the listing contract
choice_c: Section 604(6) -- failing to preserve records for three years
choice_d: Section 604(13) -- failing to disclose an ownership interest
explanation: Section 604(21) makes it a prohibited act to perform 'any act for which an appropriate real estate license is required and is not currently in effect' -- this applies even to a broker's own lapsed license, not only to unlicensed staff.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(21) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: RELRA Section 604(16) penalizes a broker's failure to adequately supervise ordinary salespersons and associate brokers. Which parallel provision penalizes a broker's failure to adequately supervise campground membership or time-share salespersons specifically?
choice_a: Section 604(27)
choice_b: Section 604(17)
choice_c: Section 604(9)
choice_d: There is no parallel provision -- Section 604(16) covers all licensee types
explanation: Section 604(27), added in 1990, separately makes it a prohibited act for a broker licensee to fail 'to exercise adequate supervision over the activities of a campground membership salesperson or a time-share salesperson' -- mirroring 604(16)'s general supervision duty for this specialized licensee category.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(16),(27) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under RELRA Section 604(31), owning an interest in a 'qualified association' becomes a prohibited act if the association does which of the following?
choice_a: Participates in prohibited acts, is not solely owned by licensees affiliated with the same broker, or holds itself out to the public as providing real estate services
choice_b: Has more than five owners
choice_c: Was formed outside Pennsylvania
choice_d: Earns more than $50,000 in a calendar year
explanation: Section 604(31) makes owning an interest in a qualified association a prohibited act when that association participates in any Section 604 prohibited act, is not solely owned by licensees all affiliated with the same broker, or holds itself out to the public as providing real estate or real estate-related services.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(31) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Notwithstanding the general rule against paying commissions to unlicensed third parties, RELRA Section 604(c) makes clear that it is NOT unlawful for a broker to do what?
choice_a: Pay a commission or compensation to a qualified association, or for an associate broker/salesperson to receive compensation from a qualified association in which they own an interest
choice_b: Pay commissions directly to a buyer's employer
choice_c: Waive Section 604(12) entirely for transactions over $1 million
choice_d: Split a commission with an out-of-state unlicensed referral agent
explanation: Section 604(c) provides that it is not unlawful for a broker to pay a commission or compensation to a qualified association, or for an associate broker or salesperson to receive compensation from a qualified association in which they own an interest -- a narrow, purpose-built exception layered onto the general commission-flow rules of Section 604(12)/(12.1).
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(c) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Per RELRA Section 201's definitions, a 'qualified association' is an entity meeting which conditions?
choice_a: It is a corporation, LLP, LP, or LLC organized under PA or other applicable law, does not itself hold a real estate license, does not hold itself out as providing real estate services, and is solely owned by licensees affiliated with the same broker
choice_b: Any LLC formed by a licensed broker for tax purposes
choice_c: A trade association of brokers recognized by the Commission
choice_d: A nonprofit consumer-advocacy group registered with the Attorney General
explanation: RELRA Section 201 defines a 'qualified association' as a corporation, limited liability partnership, limited partnership, or limited liability company that is organized under applicable law, does not hold a license under the act, does not hold itself out to the public as providing real estate or real estate-related services, and is solely owned by licensees all affiliated with the same broker.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.201 (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: How does 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 define an 'associate broker'?
choice_a: An individual broker who is employed by another broker
choice_b: A broker who has passed the exam but has fewer than 3 years' experience
choice_c: A salesperson who has completed broker-level coursework but not the broker exam
choice_d: A broker who works exclusively in commercial real estate
explanation: Section 35.201 defines 'associate broker' simply as 'an individual broker who is employed by another broker' -- someone who holds a broker's license but works under another broker rather than independently.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Per 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201, who is the 'broker of record'?
choice_a: The individual broker responsible for the real estate transactions of a partnership, association, or corporation that holds a broker's license
choice_b: The broker who has held a PA license the longest at a given firm
choice_c: Any broker named on a firm's letterhead
choice_d: The broker who personally signs every listing agreement
explanation: Section 35.201 defines 'broker of record' as 'the individual broker responsible for the real estate transactions of a partnership, association or corporation that holds a broker's license' -- the individual who bears personal accountability for an entity-licensed firm's brokerage activity.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Consistent with the exclusive-affiliation structure running throughout RELRA, how does 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 define 'salesperson'?
choice_a: An individual holding a standard or reciprocal license who is employed by a broker to perform specified licensed activities such as selling, leasing, or negotiating real estate
choice_b: Any person who has passed the salesperson exam, regardless of current employment status
choice_c: An unlicensed assistant working under a broker's direct supervision
choice_d: A person licensed to sell real estate only in a single county
explanation: Section 35.201 defines 'salesperson' as an individual holding a standard or reciprocal license 'who is employed by a broker' to sell, lease, negotiate, or otherwise perform enumerated licensed real estate activities -- reinforcing that salespersons never operate independently of a supervising broker.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: RELRA Section 606.1(a)(5) requires a licensee, as one of the non-waivable duties owed to all consumers, to do what?
choice_a: Account in a timely manner for all money and property received from or on behalf of any consumer, consistent with Section 608.5
choice_b: Personally guarantee the buyer's financing
choice_c: Waive their commission if the deal falls through
choice_d: File a copy of every listing with the county recorder of deeds
explanation: Section 606.1(a)(5) makes timely accounting for consumer money and property -- consistent with the escrow-handling rules of Section 608.5 -- one of the baseline duties every licensee owes every consumer, regardless of agency status.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.606.1(a)(5) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: When a licensee reports forming or joining a qualified association within 30 days as required by RELRA Section 606.1(a)(14), which of the following is NOT among the required disclosures?
choice_a: The qualified association's total annual gross revenue
choice_b: The name of the qualified association
choice_c: The names of the qualified association's owners
choice_d: The jurisdiction and date of the qualified association's registration
explanation: Section 606.1(a)(14) requires disclosure of the qualified association's name, its owners' names, its registration jurisdiction and date, and subsequent ownership changes -- it does not require disclosure of the association's revenue.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.606.1(a)(14) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Both RELRA Section 608.5(g) and 49 Pa. Code Section 35.325(a) require that a broker's escrow/custodial account be designated with whom as trustee?
choice_a: The broker -- never an associate broker, salesperson, or unlicensed employee
choice_b: Whichever licensee physically opened the account
choice_c: The buyer's attorney
choice_d: The bank's compliance officer
explanation: Both the statute (Section 608.5(g)) and the parallel regulation (49 Pa. Code Section 35.325(a)) require that the escrow/custodial account designate the broker -- and only the broker -- as trustee, reflecting RELRA's consistent rule that ultimate escrow accountability cannot be delegated below the broker level.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.608.5(g); 49 Pa. Code Section 35.325(a) (confirmed verbatim, both sections, via legis.state.pa.us and pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.325(a), a broker's escrow account must meet which set of requirements?
choice_a: Be maintained in a federally or state-insured bank, designate the broker as trustee, allow withdrawal without prior notice, and be used exclusively for escrow purposes
choice_b: Be co-signed by the buyer's lender
choice_c: Earn a minimum guaranteed interest rate of 2%
choice_d: Be limited to deposits under $10,000 per transaction
explanation: Section 35.325(a) sets out four escrow-account requirements: the account must be maintained in a federally or state-insured bank, designate the broker as trustee, permit withdrawal without prior notice, and be used exclusively for escrow purposes -- no other funds may share the account.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.325(a) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: A broker of record gives the office's unlicensed receptionist written authority to withdraw funds from the firm's escrow account. Is this permitted under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.325(b)?
choice_a: No -- Section 35.325(b) allows the broker to give only a licensed employee written authority to withdraw properly chargeable funds from the escrow account
choice_b: Yes, as long as the receptionist has worked there over a year
choice_c: Yes, if the broker co-signs every withdrawal
choice_d: Yes, with the Commission's advance written approval
explanation: Section 35.325(b) permits a sole-proprietor or broker-of-record to delegate escrow deposit authority to an employee, but withdrawal authority for properly chargeable funds may be given only to a licensed employee -- an unlicensed receptionist cannot lawfully hold that authority.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.325(b) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(a), the main or branch office of a broker must be under the direction and supervision of whom?
choice_a: A broker or associate broker holding either a standard or reciprocal license
choice_b: Any licensed salesperson designated as 'office manager'
choice_c: The firm's unlicensed operations manager
choice_d: No supervision requirement applies once the office is licensed
explanation: Section 35.244(a) requires that a broker's main or branch office be under the direction and supervision of a broker or associate broker holding a standard or reciprocal license -- a salesperson, regardless of title, cannot fulfill this supervisory role.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(a) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Section 35.244(c) of 49 Pa. Code requires which categories of licensee to practice in affiliation with a broker holding a standard or reciprocal license?
choice_a: Associate brokers, salespersons, cemetery salespersons, campground membership salespersons, and time-share salespersons
choice_b: Only salespersons; associate brokers may practice independently
choice_c: Only cemetery salespersons
choice_d: Only licensees with fewer than 3 years of experience
explanation: Section 35.244(c) broadly requires an associate broker, salesperson, cemetery salesperson, campground membership salesperson, or time-share salesperson to 'practice in affiliation with a broker holding either a reciprocal or standard license' -- a regulatory echo of RELRA Section 603(a)'s exclusive-affiliation rule that reaches every dependent-licensee category.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(c) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(d) prohibits a branch office from being operated in what manner?
choice_a: In a manner that permits, or is intended to permit, an employee to carry on the business of the office for the employee's sole benefit
choice_b: During hours other than 9am-5pm
choice_c: Without a fax machine on premises
choice_d: Under a name different from the main office's name
explanation: Section 35.244(d) prohibits operating a branch office in a way that lets an employee run the office purely for their own benefit -- guarding against a branch functioning as an unsupervised shadow business outside the broker's real oversight.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(d) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under RELRA Section 702(a), when can a salesperson's or associate broker's violation of the Act result in suspension or revocation of the EMPLOYING broker's own license?
choice_a: Only if it appears at a hearing that the employing broker had actual knowledge of the violation
choice_b: Automatically, any time an employee is found guilty of any violation
choice_c: Only if the broker personally committed the same type of violation previously
choice_d: Never -- brokers cannot be disciplined for employee conduct under any circumstances
explanation: Section 702(a) protects a broker from vicarious discipline: no violation by a salesperson, associate broker, or other employee is grounds for suspending or revoking the EMPLOYER's license unless it appears at the hearing that the employer had actual knowledge of the violation.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.702(a) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: How does RELRA Section 702(c) let the Commission establish that a broker had 'actual knowledge' of an employee's violation for purposes of Section 702(a)?
choice_a: A course of dealing shown to have been followed by the employee constitutes prima facie evidence of the employer's knowledge
choice_b: Actual knowledge can never be proven circumstantially -- only a signed confession suffices
choice_c: The broker is presumed to know everything any employee does, with no defense available
choice_d: Only the employee's own testimony can establish the broker's knowledge
explanation: Section 702(c) provides that a 'course of dealing shown to have been followed by such employee shall constitute prima facie evidence' of the employer's actual knowledge -- letting a pattern of conduct substitute for direct proof of what the broker specifically knew.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.702(c) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: RELRA Section 702(d) extends the same actual-knowledge protection described in Section 702(a) to which supervising relationship?
choice_a: A broker responsible for supervising a campground membership salesperson or time-share salesperson
choice_b: Only cemetery brokers supervising cemetery salespersons
choice_c: Property managers supervising maintenance staff
choice_d: No extension exists -- Section 702(a) applies only to ordinary salespersons and associate brokers
explanation: Section 702(d), added in 1990, mirrors 702(a) and (c) for the specialized licensee category: no violation by a campground membership or time-share salesperson is grounds to suspend or revoke the supervising broker's license absent actual knowledge, and a course of dealing again serves as prima facie evidence of that knowledge.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.702(d) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under RELRA Section 606, what relationship do licensees employed by a broker bear to the consumer, as a general rule?
choice_a: The same relationship the broker bears to that consumer (e.g., as seller's agent, buyer's agent, dual agent, or transaction licensee)
choice_b: No relationship at all -- only the broker has any duty to the consumer
choice_c: A relationship independent of and unrelated to the broker's own role
choice_d: A relationship that must be separately negotiated and disclosed for every individual licensee
explanation: Section 606 provides that 'licensees employed by a broker shall bear the same relationship to the consumer as the broker' -- the supervising broker's chosen role (seller's agent, buyer's agent, dual agent, or transaction licensee) generally flows down to the affiliated licensees working the transaction.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.606 (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under RELRA Section 606, even when acting as a dual agent, what designation authority does a broker retain over affiliated licensees?
choice_a: The broker may designate one licensee to act exclusively as agent of a particular seller/landlord and another to act exclusively as agent of a particular buyer/tenant
choice_b: The broker must personally handle both sides of the transaction with no delegation permitted
choice_c: The broker may designate licensees only with the Commission's prior written approval for each transaction
choice_d: Dual agency automatically strips the broker of any designation authority
explanation: Section 606 lets a broker -- including one serving as a dual agent -- designate a particular licensee to act exclusively as agent of the seller/landlord and another to act exclusively as agent of the buyer/tenant, illustrating the broker's continuing authority to structure how its affiliated licensees are deployed within a transaction.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.606 (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: RELRA Section 606.5(a)(3), governing designated agency, places what responsibility on the broker?
choice_a: The broker has the responsibility to direct and supervise the business activities of designated agents, thereby owing duties to both sides as a dual agent
choice_b: The broker has no supervisory responsibility once agents are designated -- each designated agent operates fully independently
choice_c: Only the Commission, not the broker, may direct designated agents' activities
choice_d: The responsibility to supervise designated agents may be delegated to any associate broker without restriction
explanation: Section 606.5(a)(3) makes explicit that 'a broker has the responsibility to direct and supervise the business activities of designated agents,' which is precisely why the broker (as dual agent) simultaneously owes duties to both the seller/landlord and buyer/tenant sides of a designated-agency transaction.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.606.5(a)(3) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers
question: Under RELRA Section 606.5(a)(1), what must a broker obtain before designating one or more employed licensees as the exclusive designated agent of a principal?
choice_a: The principal's written consent
choice_b: Approval from the Real Estate Commission for each designation
choice_c: A majority vote of all licensees in the office
choice_d: Nothing -- designation may occur unilaterally and orally
explanation: Section 606.5(a)(1) requires that a broker designate one or more employed licensees to serve as a principal's designated agent only 'with the written consent of the principal,' to the exclusion of the broker's other affiliated licensees.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.606.5(a)(1) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)
